title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Onboarding, Benefits, and Internal Tools
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

Welcome to Redwood. This document is the canonical company handbook page for new and existing employees covering: working model, roles and career ladders, hiring and onboarding overview, benefits and perks, and the most commonly used internal tools. The intent is to provide a single, actionable reference to get people productive and aligned with company policies.

1) Working model and expectations

- Office / remote: Redwood operates a hybrid-first model. Teams are encouraged to coordinate onsite days locally; most teams expect 1-3 onsite days/week for collaboration and all-hands.
- Core hours: There are no strict core hours, but synchronous collaboration windows are typically 10:00-16:00 PT. Check your team's working agreements.
- Communication norms: Use Slack for async and quick discussions, Confluence for long-form docs, and Gmail for external comms. Use threads and descriptive channel names; avoid multi-topic channels.
- Performance reviews: Twice-yearly (mid-year and year-end) with written feedback and calibration. Career ladders outline expectations by level (see Roles & Career Ladders).

2) Roles & career ladders (summary table)

|| Level || Typical title || Time horizon || Core expectations || Primary success metrics ||
| L1 | Associate / IC-1 | 0-1 yr | Learns codebase, contributes small features, follows design reviews | PR throughput, quality, onboarding checklist completion |
| L2 | IC / Engineer II | 1-3 yrs | Independently owns small services/features, participates in on-call | Tickets resolved, code review quality, peer feedback |
| L3 | Senior / Engineer III | 3-6 yrs | Designs subsystems, mentors others, leads medium initiatives | Project outcomes, reliability improvements, mentored hires |
| L4 | Staff / Principal | 5+ yrs | Cross-team technical leadership, sets roadmap, drives reliability/cost efficiency | System-level impact, cross-team KPIs, org health |
| L5 | Director+ | Leadership | Strategic ownership, people leadership, GTM partnership | Org outcomes, hiring velocity, retention |

- Career ladder artifacts: Each ladder includes competencies across Impact, Technical Skills, Communication, and Leadership. Teams must attach quantitative examples to promotion packets (PRs, design docs, incident ownership, mentorship).
- Promotion process: Manager initiates, candidate prepares a packet, peer reviewers assigned, final calibration with People Ops. Typical timeline is 6-10 weeks.

3) Hiring & interview process (high level)

Purpose: Evaluate role fit, technical baseline, and candidate alignment with Redwood values. Summary steps:

1. Requisition & hiring plan created by manager + People Ops (includes role spec, title, pay band).
2. Sourcing & outreach (Recruiting owns screening).
3. Phone screen (Recruiter + Hiring Manager) - culture and baseline fit.
4. Technical interview loop: coding/design/problem-solving + take-home for senior roles.
5. Final on-site / virtual loop: cross-functional stakeholders and manager deep dive.
6. Offer & negotiation handled by Recruiting + People Ops.
7. Reference checks and background screening.

Hiring SLA targets: screen-to-offer within 28 days for critical roles; average time-to-fill target is 45 days. Hiring managers should ensure interview feedback is submitted within 48 hours.

4) New hire onboarding: checklist and timeline

Pre-day 1 (People Ops + IT):
- Create employee record in HRIS (Greenhouse/Workday).
- Provision accounts: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence, GitHub, Jira, internal AWS account, 1Password vault.
- Order equipment (laptop, monitor, dongles) per Equipment Policy.

Day 1-7 (Orientation & safety):
1. Welcome session with People Ops (benefits overview, payroll setup).
2. Security & compliance training (must be completed within 3 days).
3. Team onboarding: meet manager, 1:1s with key cross-functional partners.
4. Complete role-specific quickstarts (codebase walkthrough, local dev setup).

30/60/90 day plan (typical manager expectations):
- 30 days: productive locally, first small ticket merged, completed security training.
- 60 days: owning a small feature, first on-call shadowing.
- 90 days: full contributor on team roadmap, performance check-in.

Onboarding checklist (condensed):
- Accounts provisioned and MFA enabled.
- Codebase builds locally.
- First PR merged and reviewed.
- Security & privacy training completed.
- Benefits enrollment completed within 30 days.

Security & access steps (numbered):
1. Complete Security Awareness training (link in IT onboarding).
2. Request elevated access via Access Request form (link in Confluence).
3. Manager approval required for production AWS/GCP access.

5) Benefits & perks (summary)

- Health: Medical/dental/vision plans with company contribution; flexible spending accounts (FSA).
- Parental leave: Primary caregiver paid leave (16 weeks), secondary caregiver paid leave (8 weeks).
- Time off: 20 vacation days + 10 company holidays + floating wellness days. Unused vacation encouraged to be taken; accruals follow policy in payroll.
- Retirement: 401(k) with company match up to 4%.
- Compensation and equity: Competitive salary bands and annual calibration; equity grants for full-time hires (more details in offer letter).
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual L&D budget + internal learning stipends for conferences.
- Additional perks: commuter stipend (region-specific), mental health benefits, monthly wellness stipend, team offsites budget.

Benefits administration: People Ops handles enrollments. New hires must complete elections within 30 days. For detailed plan documents and carriers see the Benefits space in Confluence.

6) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

- Okta: Single sign-on for company apps. Enrollment required on day 0.
- Google Workspace: Email, Calendar, Drive. Shared drives for teams.
- Slack: Primary messaging. Use #team-name channels and #all-hands for company announcements. Pin key docs and set channel topics.
- Confluence: Primary knowledge base. Use team-spaces for owned content. Pages should follow the company doc template (Summary, Owners, Dates, Action items).
- GitHub: Code hosting. All production changes require PRs, 2 reviewers for critical repos. Branch protection rules enforced.
- Jira: Issue tracking. Use component labels and link PRs to Jira tickets.
- 1Password: Secrets management for team vaults. Rotate secrets per policy and request access via 1Password groups.
- AWS console / GCP console: Production access requires manager approval and SSO onboarding; use least privilege.

Sample CLI/commands for common tasks:
- Git clone: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/your-repo.git
- Create branch: git checkout -b feat/your-feature
- Submit PR: hub pull-request -b main -m "Short summary"

7) On-call and incident expectations (summary)

- Who: Most engineers will take on-call rotations; managers will coordinate schedules.
- Responsibilities: Triage alerts, restore service or escalate, write post-incident notes.
- Escalation: Pager -> primary on-call -> secondary -> SRE lead. See Incident Response runbook for full steps.
- Postmortems: All SEV1/SEV2 incidents require a postmortem posted to confluence/incidents and a 2-week follow-up on remediation progress.

8) Equipment & reimbursement

- Standard equipment: MacBook Pro (or equivalent), 2 x 27" external monitors, keyboard and mouse. Exceptions are supported; discuss with People Ops.
- Reimbursement: Approved home-office purchases up to $500 covered with receipt submission.

9) People Ops ownership and contacts

- People Ops (primary): people-ops@redwood.ai
- IT support: it-support@redwood.ai (ticket via Slack #it-support)
- Benefits & payroll: payroll@redwood.ai
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.ai

10) FAQs and troubleshooting

Q: Who sets my hybrid schedule?
A: Your manager and team set expectations; check team handbook pages for local norms.

Q: What if I need immediate time off for family emergency?
A: Discuss with your manager and People Ops. Redwood supports emergency leave per policy.

Q: How do I request headcount or role changes on my team?
A: Submit a hiring plan with the manager and People Ops; follow the hiring intake template.

11) Related policies and templates

- Equipment policy: /confluence/policies-and-process/equipment-policy
- Security & access: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth
- Hiring intake template: /confluence/product-docs/requirements/hiring-intake-template

12) Document maintenance and owners

- Owner: People Ops (Asha Patel).
- Review cadence: Annual review in January; interim updates as policy changes.
- How to propose updates: Create a Confluence page edit and notify the owner; major policy changes must be reviewed by People Ops and Legal.

Appendix: 90-day manager checklist (numbered)
1. Set clear 30/60/90 goals on day 1.
2. Introduce new hire to cross-functional partners in week 1.
3. Ensure access required for role is provisioned by day 3.
4. Schedule weekly 1:1s for first 90 days.
5. Provide first performance feedback at 30 days and formal check-in at 90 days.
